headline: High risk of filesystem-based prompt injection and cascading errors; medium data-leak and capability-conflict exposure from shared files and broad egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads and writes files and shares state via filesystem, while next-ai-draw-io ingests files and uses natural-language commands with MCP/browser access. That creates a plausible file-mediated injection path even without a direct bridge. The pair is not documented together, so uncertainty pushes upward from low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF next-ai-draw-io parses file contents as instructions or prompts
IF Mentat writes attacker-controlled text into files later opened by next-ai-draw-io
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted files
Require manual review before opening files produced by the other agent
Prefix exchanged files with a non-executable format and provenance note
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat has broad network egress and handles model-provider API keys; next-ai-draw-io also has broad egress, multiple model backends, and MCP. If they share a workspace, sensitive source code or embedded secrets can flow from one agent into the other and then out to third-party APIs. The pairwise interaction is undocumented, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF the agents share files containing source code or secrets
IF next-ai-draw-io sends file contents to a remote model backend
IF Mentat reads files that include credentials or private code
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared files
Use separate API keys per agent
Restrict both agents to a local-only model during shared tasks
Review outbound requests before enabling remote models
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can modify git state and write the filesystem; next-ai-draw-io can use MCP and broad network egress. If both touch the same repository or mutable workspace, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt git state. No locking is documented, so the safest reading is a real default-path conflict rather than a read-only overlap.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or directory
IF edits occur concurrently without external locking
IF MCP tools mutate files or project state
mitigations: Assign one writer at a time
Use git branches per agent
Add a manual merge step after each agent run
Pause one agent while the other is editing
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional workspace coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and next-ai-draw-io uses natural-language commands and AI-assisted visualization. If next-ai-draw-io treats Mentat's generated text or diffs as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect diagrams or actions. Because the pair is undocumented, uncertainty again favors the higher severity over low.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io consumes Mentat output without verification
IF Mentat-generated diffs are converted into diagram content or actions
IF no human review occurs between generation and downstream use
mitigations: Require explicit verification before downstream use
Compare outputs against source files manually
Limit downstream actions to preview mode
Annotate generated artifacts as untrusted
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and touch files plus API keys, but the profiles do not show a residency mismatch, regulated data class, or conflicting retention policy. The main compliance concern is generic secret handling, which is not enough for medium under this rubric. The other agent is not separately cited because no distinct compliance surface is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into either agent
IF the deployment region or retention policy differs between the two backends
IF API keys are stored in shared project files
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workspaces
Confirm retention settings for each backend
Store API keys in separate secret managers
Review data-processing terms for each model provider
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls
